shared.surfBiteReport: The most recent Half Hitch PCB report (July 31, 2026 — five days ago) describes the surf as the bright spot of the week despite generally stained, weather-stirred water following Tropical Storm Bertha. A handful of pompano and Spanish mackerel were still being caught, though baitfish counts along the beach remain below pre-storm levels and additional wind and rain over the weekend could slow recovery. Redfish are responding well to the full moon, moving up in the water column on outgoing tides — floating plugs and large soft plastics are the recommended approach. With water temps at 85°F, pompano activity is typically reduced compared to spring peaks, but charter reports from mid-July showed exceptional pompano numbers before the storm; expect that bite to rebuild as conditions clear. The key right now is scouting for clean, grass-free water before committing — sargassum and storm turbidity are the main obstacles along the 30A-to-PCB stretch.
